explanation: Brazil has no special taboo around the head the way Thailand does. Patting an adult you don't know well on the head can still come across as patronizing or overly familiar, much as it would in most Western cultures, but it is not treated as a deep cultural offense. It's fine with children or very close friends.
local_tip: Save head-pats for children or close friends; greet adults with a handshake, cheek kiss, or a pat on the shoulder/back instead.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred part of the body, and touching it is a serious taboo.
Patting a child's head is often affectionate, but doing so to an adult can read as patronizing.
Patting an adult's head is normally reserved for close friends or family; in professional settings it can seem condescending.

sources.title: Brazilian Culture - Etiquette, The Cultural Atlas
